en.title: Saddleback Mountain 20 cm: freezing level climbs above the peaks
en.description: Rain threatens upper slopes at Saddleback Mountain where 20 cm sits at 1,218 m. Freezing level rises to 3,760 m today, 22 November.
en.lede: Saddleback Mountain holds the deepest snow in the Northeast at 20 cm on its upper slopes, but today's warm air mass is pushing the freezing level well above the summits. Rain will fall across all elevations where your skis travel, turning what little snow exists into slush and exposing rock by mid-afternoon.

p: Of 112 resorts tracked across the Northeast, only 31 have measurable snow cover on 22 November. Saddleback Mountain leads with 20 cm at its top at 1,218 m (4,000 ft), while Cannon Mountain holds 16 cm. This is thinner than usual for late November—at this height and date, we normally see around 6 cm, so conditions are well below the seasonal average. The snow that remains is fragmented and patchy, concentrated only on the highest terrain.

Lower elevations have already turned bare. Our model shows zero depth at the base of every major resort. The satellite last confirmed snow at Cannon Mountain on 20 November, but most other peaks showed nothing. This early-season snow arrived with little water content and weak bonding; it has not consolidated into stable coverage.

sections.h: Rain replaces snow from summit to base
p: The freezing level today rises to 3,760 m (12,330 ft) at its daily high—far above even Saddleback's summit. This means rain, not snow, falls across your entire vertical drop. The boundary between wet and dry air passes through the mid-troposphere, well above the ski terrain. Water will soak into the existing snow patches, collapse the weak early-season structure, and expose subsurface rock within hours.

By tomorrow, 23 November, the freezing level drops sharply to between 260 m and 3,010 m, bringing genuine cold air back into the mountains. Snow may fall on the highest slopes of Saddleback and Cannon, but only 5–8 cm is forecast over the next seven days—too little to rebuild coverage after today's rain damage.

North-facing terrain and elevations above 1,100 m will shed rain somewhat faster than south or west aspects, simply because they receive less direct solar heating. Saddleback's peak at 1,218 m will likely retain patches of wet snow longest into the afternoon, but the word 'retain' is generous—these patches will be thin, waterlogged, and hiding rock.

The base areas and mid-mountain zones are already bare down to grass and dirt. Groomed runs at lower elevations have no snow to ski; upper runs may offer a few metres of skiable terrain if you pick the coldest north-facing pitches and reach them before 14:00 local time.

sections.h: What the model shows for the coming week
p: By 25 November, snow-covered area across the entire Northeast falls from the current 1,050 km² to just 340 km², and only 19 of 112 resorts retain any white. The region is entering a marginal early-season window. Fresh snow totals of 2–8 cm are scattered and meagre; most will fall at night and vanish within 36 hours if air temperatures climb again.

The comparison to past winters is sobering: at Saddleback, our model shows 2 cm of snow at 936 m today, which is deeper than only 15 of the past 46 November 22nds. This ranks in roughly the lower third of historical conditions for this date.

sections.h: What to do on the mountain today
p: If you are aiming to ski, pick Saddleback or Cannon and climb to the highest groomed runs before 10:00. Rain will be arriving during the morning and intensifying. Stay on prepared pistes—early-season snow is thin and rocks lie beneath—and descend before the slush becomes unmanageable. Check the resort website for lift operations; many mountains have limited lifts running in marginal coverage like this.

Avoid off-piste terrain entirely. Early-season snow lacks structure, rocks are barely covered, and wet snow on a thin base creates avalanche risk. Read the official Northeast avalanche bulletin before considering any steep ungroomed slopes, though today is not a day for it.

advice: Ski the highest north-facing groomed terrain at Saddleback or Cannon Mountain before 10:00 today; rain will soak everything by mid-morning and expose rock within hours.
Stay on marked runs only. The 20 cm at Saddleback's top masks bare ground below—rocks are your enemy on thin early-season coverage.
Check the official Northeast avalanche bulletin before considering any off-piste; wet snow bonding poorly to thin base increases slide risk.
Head down by 14:00. Afternoon rain will turn the slush into a unrideable crust and expose all hazards. Conditions will degrade steadily.
Verify lift status on the resort website before you go. Marginal snow cover may mean limited operations or closure of some terrain.

captions.map: Snow depth across the Northeast on 22 November 2026, showing concentration at highest elevations. Only 31 of 112 resorts hold any snow; Saddleback Mountain leads at 20 cm at 1,218 m. Freezing level today reaches 3,760 m, bringing rain across all ski terrain.
